p.src: The man who offered this counsel was Sun Zi, Minister of the Secretariat. Cao Rui asked, “What ingenious plan have you?” Sun Zi memorialized: “When Emperor Wu, our Great Progenitor, conquered Zhang Lu, he first faced grave danger before ultimately succeeding. He once told his ministers, ‘The land of Nanzheng is truly a prison fashioned by Heaven.’ The road through Xie Valley consists of five hundred li of rocky caverns and is no ground for the use of arms. If we now raise all the troops in the realm to attack Shu, Eastern Wu will invade us once more. It would be better to divide our present forces among the great commanders, have them hold the strategic passes, and conserve their strength. Within a few years, the Central Realm will grow stronger by the day, while Wu and Shu will surely wear each other down. Would not striking them then assure our victory?” I beg Your Majesty to decide.” Cao Rui then asked Sima Yi, “What do you think of this argument?” Sima Yi replied, “Minister Sun’s words are entirely sound.” Cao Rui accepted the counsel and ordered Sima Yi to assign the generals to guard the strategic passes. Leaving Guo Huai and Zhang He to defend Chang’an, he richly rewarded the three armies and returned in his imperial carriage to Luoyang.

p.src: Meanwhile, Kongming returned to Hanzhong and counted his troops. Only Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi were missing, which greatly troubled him. He therefore ordered Guan Xing and Zhang Bao each to lead a force to their aid. Just as the two were about to depart, a report came that Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi had arrived without losing a single man or horse. Nor had any baggage or equipment been abandoned. Overjoyed, Kongming personally led the generals out to welcome them. Zhao Yun hurriedly dismounted, prostrated himself, and said, “Why should the Prime Minister come so far to welcome a defeated general?” Kongming quickly helped him up, took his hand, and said, “It was my failure to distinguish the worthy from the foolish that brought this about! Troops and commanders everywhere suffered losses; you alone, Zilong, did not lose a single man or horse. How did you manage it?” Deng Zhi explained, “I led the troops ahead, while Zilong alone covered the rear. He slew enemy commanders and won such distinction that the foe was terrified. Thus none of our military stores or other possessions had to be abandoned.” Kongming said, “A true general indeed!” He then brought out fifty jin of gold to present to Zhao Yun, and another ten thousand bolts of silk to reward Zhao Yun’s soldiers. Zhao Yun declined, saying, “The army has achieved not the slightest merit, and all of us bear guilt. If we were rewarded instead, the Prime Minister’s rewards and punishments would be unjust. Please store these in the treasury for now and bestow them upon the troops this coming winter. It will not be too late.” Kongming sighed, “When the late Emperor lived, he often praised Zilong’s virtue. Today you have proved him right!” Thereafter his esteem and respect for Zhao Yun increased twofold.

p.src: Suddenly word came that Ma Su, Wang Ping, Wei Yan, and Gao Xiang had arrived. Kongming first summoned Wang Ping into his tent and rebuked him: “I ordered you and Ma Su to defend Jieting together. Why did you not remonstrate with him and so prevent this disaster?” Wang Ping replied, “I urged him again and again to build an earthen fort beside the main road and defend it. But the Army Adviser flew into a rage and refused. I therefore led five thousand men away and encamped ten li from the mountain. The Wei troops suddenly arrived and surrounded the mountain on all four sides. I led my men in more than ten assaults, but each time failed to break through. The next day, the army collapsed utterly, and countless men surrendered. My isolated force could not hold its ground, so I went to Wei Wenchang for aid. Halfway there, Wei troops trapped us in a valley, but I fought desperately and broke free. By the time I returned to my camp, the Wei troops had already seized it. When I headed for Lieliu, I met Gao Xiang on the road. We then divided our forces into three columns to raid the Wei camp, hoping to recover Jieting. But when I saw no ambush force along the road to Jieting, I became suspicious. Climbing to high ground and looking out, I saw Wei Yan and Gao Xiang surrounded by Wei troops. I immediately fought my way into the encirclement, rescued both generals, and joined them with the Army Adviser. Fearing that Yangping Pass might be lost, I hastened back to defend it. It is not true that I failed to remonstrate with him. If the Prime Minister does not believe me, he may question the officers of every division.”

p.src: Kongming shouted for Wang Ping to withdraw, then summoned Ma Su into the tent. Ma Su came bound and knelt before it. Kongming’s countenance changed as he said, “From childhood you have read the military classics deeply and mastered the methods of war. I repeatedly warned you that Jieting was the foundation of my whole campaign, and you pledged the lives of your entire family when accepting this grave responsibility. Had you listened to Wang Ping from the start, how could this disaster have occurred? Now the army has been defeated, commanders lost, territory abandoned, and cities taken—all through your fault! If military law is not openly and properly enforced, how can the troops be made to obey? You have broken the law; do not resent me for what follows. After your death, I shall provide your wife and children with grain stipends every month. You need not worry for them.” He ordered the attendants to drag Ma Su out and behead him. Ma Su wept and said, “The Prime Minister has treated me as a son, and I have regarded you as a father. I truly cannot escape the death penalty. I only beg the Prime Minister to remember how Emperor Shun punished Gun yet employed Yu. Then, though I die, I shall bear no grievance even in the netherworld!” When he had finished, he wept bitterly. Kongming brushed away his tears and said, “You and I have shared the affection of brothers. Your son shall be as my own son. You need say no more.”

p.src: The attendants dragged Ma Su beyond the camp gate and prepared to behead him. At that moment, the Army Adviser Jiang Wan arrived from Chengdu. Seeing the warriors about to execute Ma Su, he was greatly alarmed and shouted for them to spare the man. He went in to see Kongming and said, “When Chu put Dechen to death in former times, Duke Wen rejoiced. The realm is not yet settled; is it not a great pity to execute a man of wisdom and strategy?” Kongming answered through flowing tears, “Sun Wu was able to prevail throughout the realm in former times because his enforcement of the law was clear. Now the four quarters are in turmoil and warfare has only just begun. If we cast aside the law, how can we punish the rebels? He must be beheaded.” Before long, the warriors presented Ma Su’s head below the steps. Kongming wept without cease. Jiang Wan asked, “Now that Youchang has been punished according to military law for his offense, why does the Prime Minister weep?” Kongming replied, “I do not weep for Ma Su. I remember how, when the late Emperor lay near death in Baidi, he warned me: ‘Ma Su’s words exceed his true abilities; he must not be entrusted with great responsibility.’ Today his words have indeed come true. I bitterly regret my own lack of discernment and, recalling the late Emperor’s wisdom, can only weep in anguish!” Every officer and soldier, high and low, shed tears. p.src: When the Latter Lord had finished reading, he said, “Victory and defeat are common fortunes of war. Why should the Prime Minister speak thus?” Palace Attendant Fei Yi memorialized, “I have heard that those who govern a state must place the observance of law above all else. If the law is not enforced, how can the people be made to obey? The Prime Minister suffered defeat and has requested his own demotion; this is altogether proper.” The Latter Lord accepted this counsel and issued an edict demoting Kongming to General of the Right, while allowing him to perform the duties of Prime Minister and command the troops as before. He then ordered Fei Yi to carry the edict to Hanzhong. After Kongming had received the edict of demotion, Fei Yi feared that he might feel ashamed and so congratulated him, saying, “The people of Shu are delighted to learn that the Prime Minister initially captured four counties.” Kongming’s expression changed. “What manner of words are these? To gain territory only to lose it again is no different from never gaining it at all. For you to congratulate me on this only deepens my shame.” Fei Yi continued, “I recently heard that His Majesty was greatly pleased by the Prime Minister’s acquisition of Jiang Wei.” Kongming said angrily, “I returned with a defeated army without having taken a single inch of land. This is my grave offense. What loss is one Jiang Wei to Wei?” Fei Yi asked again, “The Prime Minister now commands several hundred thousand mighty troops. Might you campaign against Wei once more?” Kongming replied, “When our great army was stationed at Qishan and Jigu, our troops outnumbered the enemy, yet we could not defeat them and were instead defeated ourselves. The fault lies not in the number of soldiers but in their commander. I now intend to reduce the troops and officers, enforce punishments clearly, reflect upon my errors, and seek adaptable methods for the future. Otherwise, what use are troops, however numerous? Henceforth, all who cherish far-reaching concerns for the state need only diligently attack my faults and rebuke my shortcomings. Then our affairs may be settled, the enemy destroyed, and success awaited in the near future.” Fei Yi and all the generals were convinced by his reasoning. Fei Yi then returned to Chengdu. In Hanzhong, Kongming cared for his soldiers and cherished the people, trained the troops and instructed them in warfare, constructed equipment for attacking cities and crossing rivers, amassed provisions and fodder, and prepared battle rafts for future designs. Wei spies learned of this and reported it to Luoyang.

p.src: When Cao Rui, ruler of Wei, heard the report, he immediately summoned Sima Yi to discuss a plan for conquering Shu. Sima Yi said, “Shu cannot yet be attacked. The weather is now fiercely hot, so the Shu army certainly will not march out. If our army penetrates deeply into their territory, they will hold the strategic defiles, which cannot be taken quickly.” Cao Rui asked, “What are we to do if their army invades again?” Sima Yi replied, “I have already determined that Zhuge Liang will next imitate Han Xin’s stratagem of secretly crossing by Chencang. I shall recommend one man to go to the mouth of the Chencang road, build a fortress, and defend it. Then nothing can go amiss. He stands nine chi tall, has the arms of an ape, excels at archery, and possesses profound strategy. If Zhuge Liang invades, this man alone will be sufficient to withstand him.” Cao Rui was delighted and asked, “Who is this man?” Sima Yi memorialized, “He is a native of Taiyuan, surnamed Hao, named Zhao, and styled Bodao. He now serves as General of Miscellaneous Pacification and guards Hexi.” Cao Rui accepted the proposal and promoted Hao Bodao to General Who Guards the West. He ordered him to guard the mouth of the Chencang road. An envoy was dispatched with the edict.

p.src: Suddenly a report arrived that Cao Xiu, Grand Commander of the Yangzhou forces, had submitted a memorial stating that Zhou Fang, Administrator of Shenyang in Eastern Wu, wished to surrender his commandery and had secretly sent a man to set forth seven points. The message declared that Eastern Wu could be destroyed and requested that troops be sent swiftly to seize it. Cao Rui opened the memorial upon his imperial couch and read it together with Sima Yi. Sima Yi memorialized, “These words are most reasonable. Wu is destined to perish. I am willing to lead an army to assist Cao Xiu.” Suddenly, one man among the ranks of officials memorialized, “The words of men of Wu are changeable and inconsistent and cannot be deeply trusted. Zhou Fang is a man of wisdom and strategy; he would surely never surrender. This is merely a deceitful scheme to lure our troops.” All looked toward him and saw that it was Jia Kui, General Who Establishes Might. Sima Yi said, “These words cannot be disregarded either, but neither can this opportunity be allowed to slip away.” The ruler of Wei said, “Zhongda and Jia Kui may go together to assist Cao Xiu.” The two accepted the order and departed. Thereupon Cao Xiu led the main army straight toward Wancheng, while Jia Kui led the Vanguard General Man Chong and Hu Zhi, Administrator of Dongwan, directly toward Yangcheng and onward to Dongguan. Sima Yi led his own troops straight toward Jiangling.

p.src: Meanwhile Sun Quan, ruler of Wu, was at Dongguan in Wuchang. He assembled his officials and said, “Zhou Fang, Administrator of Poyang, has sent a secret memorial reporting that Cao Xiu, Wei’s Commander of Yangzhou, intends to invade. Zhou Fang has therefore devised a ruse, secretly setting forth seven points to lure the Wei army deep into perilous ground, where we may ambush and capture it. Now the Wei forces are advancing by three routes. What wise counsel have you?” Gu Yong stepped forward and said, “None but Lu Boyan is equal to this great responsibility.” Sun Quan was delighted. He summoned Lu Xun, appointed him Great General Who Supports the State and Supreme Marshal Who Pacifies the North, placed the great imperial army under his command, and authorized him to exercise the ruler’s powers. He bestowed upon him the white yak-tail standard and yellow battle-axe, and ordered every civil and military official to obey his commands. Sun Quan personally held Lu Xun’s whip for him. After accepting the command and offering thanks for the favor, Lu Xun recommended two men as commanders of his left and right wings, intending to divide the troops to meet the enemy’s three routes. Sun Quan asked who they were. Lu Xun replied, “General of Rousing Might Zhu Huan and General Who Pacifies the South Quan Cong may serve as my assistants.” Sun Quan agreed and at once appointed Zhu Huan Commander of the Left and Quan Cong Commander of the Right. Thus Lu Xun assumed overall command of more than seven hundred thousand troops from the eighty-one prefectures south of the Yangtze and from Jing and the lake country. With Zhu Huan on the left, Quan Cong on the right, and Lu Xun himself in the center, the three armies advanced. Zhu Huan proposed a plan: “Cao Xiu holds office only because he is an imperial kinsman; he is no commander of wisdom or courage. Now he has heeded Zhou Fang’s enticing words and penetrated deep into perilous ground. If the Marshal attacks him, Cao Xiu will surely be defeated. After his defeat he must flee by one of two roads: Jiashi on the left or Guiche on the right. Both are remote mountain paths of the greatest steepness and danger. I ask leave to lead one force while Quan Zihuang leads another, and to lie in ambush among the mountain defiles. If we first block the roads with timber and great rocks, Cao Xiu can be captured. Once Cao Xiu is captured, we may drive straight onward, take Shouchun as easily as turning a hand, and threaten Xu and Luoyang. Such an opportunity comes but once in ten thousand generations.” Lu Xun said, “That is not a sound plan. I have a subtle design of my own.” Zhu Huan withdrew, nursing resentment. Lu Xun ordered Zhuge Jin and the others to hold Jiangling against Sima Yi. The forces on every route were duly assigned and made ready.

After his defeat he must flee by one of two roads: Jiashi on the left or Guiche on the right.
Both are remote mountain paths of the greatest steepness and danger.
I ask leave to lead one force while Quan Zihuang leads another, and to lie in ambush among the mountain defiles. If we first block the roads with timber and great rocks, Cao Xiu can be captured.
Once Cao Xiu is captured, we may drive straight onward, take Shouchun as easily as turning a hand, and threaten Xu and Luoyang. Such an opportunity comes but once in ten thousand generations.”
Lu Xun said, “That is not a sound plan. I have a subtle design of my own.”
Zhu Huan withdrew, nursing resentment.
Lu Xun ordered Zhuge Jin and the others to hold Jiangling against Sima Yi.
The forces on every route were duly assigned and made ready.

p.src: Meanwhile, Cao Xiu’s army approached Wancheng. Zhou Fang came out to meet him and went directly to Cao Xiu’s tent. Cao Xiu asked, “I recently received your letter. The seven points you set forth were most reasonable, and I reported them to the Son of Heaven. Hence this great army has advanced by three routes. If we obtain the lands east of the Yangtze, your merit will be considerable. Some say that you are a man of many stratagems and fear that your words may not be true. But I believe that you would never deceive me.” Zhou Fang burst into tears, snatched the sword worn by one of his attendants, and tried to cut his own throat, but Cao Xiu hastily stopped him. Holding the sword, Zhou Fang said, “In setting forth those seven points, I regretted only that I could not tear out my heart and liver to show my sincerity. Now doubts have arisen instead; surely some man of Wu has employed a scheme to sow discord. If their words are believed, I shall surely die. Heaven alone can attest to my loyal heart!” When he had finished speaking, he again attempted to cut his own throat. Cao Xiu was greatly alarmed. He hurriedly seized Zhou Fang and said, “I was only jesting. Why do you act like this?” Zhou Fang then cut off his hair with the sword, cast it upon the ground, and said, “I have treated you with a loyal heart, yet you make sport of me. I cut off this hair bequeathed to me by my parents to make my sincerity known.”

p.src: Cao Xiu believed him completely and gave a banquet in his honor. When the feast was over, Zhou Fang took his leave. Suddenly it was reported that Jia Kui, General Who Establishes Might, had come to see him. Cao Xiu ordered him admitted and asked, “Why have you come?” Jia Kui said, “I judge that Eastern Wu’s forces must all be stationed at Wancheng. Commander, you must not advance rashly. Wait until I join you in a pincer attack, and the enemy can be defeated.” Cao Xiu angrily replied, “Are you trying to rob me of my achievement?” Jia Kui said, “I have also heard that Zhou Fang cut off his hair to seal his oath, but that is a deception. In former days, Yaoli cut off his own arm before assassinating Qingji. Zhou Fang must not be trusted too deeply.” Cao Xiu flew into a rage. “Just as I am about to raise the army, why do you speak such words to undermine my troops’ morale?” He shouted to his attendants to drag Jia Kui out and behead him. The officers pleaded, “It would bode ill for the army to execute a great general before the campaign has even begun. We beg you to spare him for the present.” Cao Xiu consented. He kept Jia Kui’s troops in camp for reassignment and personally led an army to seize Dongguan. When Zhou Fang learned that Jia Kui had been stripped of his command, he secretly rejoiced. “Had Cao Xiu followed Jia Kui’s advice, Eastern Wu would have been defeated! Now Heaven has granted me success!” He immediately sent a man secretly to Wancheng to inform Lu Xun. Lu Xun summoned his officers and issued his commands. “Shiting lies ahead. Though the road runs through the hills, it offers ample ground for an ambush. Go swiftly and occupy the broad ground at Shiting, deploy in battle formation, and await the Wei army.” He then appointed Xu Sheng as vanguard and ordered him to lead the troops forward.

p.src: Meanwhile, Cao Xiu ordered Zhou Fang to guide the army forward. As they marched, Cao Xiu asked, “What place lies ahead?” Zhou Fang replied, “Shiting lies ahead. It is suitable for encampment.” Cao Xiu followed his advice and led the whole army, together with its wagons, weapons, and other equipment, to encamp at Shiting. The next day, scouts reported, “An unknown number of Wu troops have occupied the mountain pass ahead.” Cao Xiu was greatly alarmed. “Zhou Fang said there were no troops. Why, then, are they prepared for us?” He urgently sought Zhou Fang to question him, but was told that Zhou Fang had taken several dozen men and vanished no one knew where. Cao Xiu bitterly regretted his error. “I have fallen into the enemy’s trap! Even so, there is nothing to fear.” He appointed the general Zhang Pu as vanguard and sent him with several thousand troops to engage the Wu army. When the two armies had drawn up opposite each other, Zhang Pu rode out and shouted, “Enemy general, surrender at once!” Xu Sheng rode out to meet him. After they had fought many bouts, Zhang Pu could hold out no longer. He reined in his horse, withdrew his troops, and returned to Cao Xiu, reporting that Xu Sheng’s valor was irresistible. Cao Xiu said, “I shall defeat him with a stratagem.” He ordered Zhang Pu to lead twenty thousand troops into ambush south of Shiting. He also ordered Xue Qiao to lead twenty thousand troops into ambush north of Shiting. “Tomorrow I shall personally lead one thousand troops to challenge the enemy, then feign defeat and lure them before the northern hills. When the cannon sounds as the signal, we shall attack from three sides and surely win a great victory. The two generals accepted the plan, and that night each led twenty thousand troops away to lie in ambush.

p.src: Meanwhile, Lu Xun summoned Zhu Huan and Quan Cong and instructed them, “Each of you is to lead thirty thousand troops around the hills at Shiting to the rear of Cao Xiu’s camp, then set fires as the signal. I shall personally lead the main army up the central route, and Cao Xiu can then be captured.” At dusk that day, the two generals accepted their orders and advanced with their troops. During the second watch, Zhu Huan’s force had just circled behind the Wei camp when it encountered Zhang Pu’s ambush. Zhang Pu did not realize they were Wu troops and came straight over to question them, whereupon Zhu Huan cut him down from his horse with a single stroke. The Wei troops fled, and Zhu Huan ordered his rear ranks to set fires. Quan Cong’s force circled behind the Wei camp and ran straight into Xue Qiao’s formation, where a fierce slaughter ensued. Xue Qiao fled in defeat. The Wei troops suffered grievous losses and raced back to their main camp. Behind them, Zhu Huan and Quan Cong attacked along their two routes. Cao Xiu’s camp fell into utter confusion, and his own troops collided with one another. Cao Xiu hastily mounted and fled toward the Jiashi road. Xu Sheng led a great body of troops down the main road in pursuit. Countless Wei soldiers were killed, while those fleeing for their lives cast away all their armor and clothing. Greatly alarmed, Cao Xiu raced desperately along the Jiashi road. Suddenly a body of troops burst from a side path. The general at their head was none other than Jia Kui. Cao Xiu’s panic eased somewhat, and he said in shame, “I did not heed your counsel, and now I have indeed suffered this defeat!” Jia Kui said, “Commander, you must leave this road quickly. If the Wu troops block it with timber and rocks, we shall all be in peril!” Cao Xiu thereupon spurred his horse onward while Jia Kui guarded the rear. In thickly wooded places and along steep, narrow paths, Jia Kui planted many banners to create the illusion of hidden troops. When Xu Sheng arrived in pursuit and glimpsed the corners of banners showing below the hillside, he suspected an ambush and dared not pursue farther, but withdrew his troops and returned. Thus Cao Xiu was saved. When Sima Yi learned of Cao Xiu’s defeat, he too withdrew his army.

p.src: Meanwhile, Lu Xun was awaiting news of victory. Before long, Xu Sheng, Zhu Huan, and Quan Cong all arrived. The captured wagons, arms, cattle, horses, donkeys, mules, military supplies, and equipment were beyond counting, and more than ten thousand soldiers had surrendered. Lu Xun was overjoyed and, together with Governor Zhou Fang and all the generals, withdrew the army and returned to Wu. Sun Quan, ruler of Wu, led his civil and military officials out of Wuchang to welcome them, and held the imperial canopy over Lu Xun as they entered the city. All the generals received promotions and rewards. Seeing Zhou Fang without his hair, Sun Quan comforted and praised him. “You cut off your hair to accomplish this great undertaking. Your merit and fame deserve to be inscribed in the annals.” He immediately enfeoffed Zhou Fang as Marquis Within the Passes and held a grand banquet to reward the army and celebrate the victory. Lu Xun submitted, “Cao Xiu has now suffered a crushing defeat, and the Wei troops have lost heart. You should compose a state letter and send an envoy into Shu, instructing Zhuge Liang to advance and attack them.” Sun Quan followed his advice and sent an envoy bearing the letter into Shu. Indeed:
